papers.title: The synergistic effect of strontium-substituted hydroxyapatite and microRNA-21 on improving bone remodeling and osseointegration.
papers.abstract: Surgical failure, mainly caused by loosening implants, causes great mental and physical trauma to patients. As the population ages, improving the physicochemical properties of implants to achieve favourable osseointegration will continue to be the focus of future research. Herein, we fabricated a titanium (Ti)-based SrHA/miR-21 composite coating that was generated by hydrothermal deposition of SrHA followed by miR-21 nanocapsule immobilisation. Both SrHA nanoparticles with good superhydrophilicity and miR-21 nanocapsules with uniform sizes were distributed evenly on the surface of Ti. In vitro experiments revealed that the composite coating was beneficial for osteoblast proliferation, differentiation and mineralization. In vivo evaluations demonstrated that this coating could not only promote the expression of the angiogenic factor CD31 but also enhance the expression of osteoblastic genes to facilitate angio-osteogenesis. In addition, the composite coating also showed a decreased RANKL expression compared with the miR-21 coating. As a result, the SrHA/miR-21 composite coating promoted new bone formation and mineralization and thus enhanced osseointegration and bone-implant bonding strength. Therefore, this method provides a new strategy for bone repair.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过复合涂层改善钛植入体的骨整合，减少植入失败。
summary_zh.method: 水热沉积锶取代羟基磷灰石并固定miR-21纳米胶囊制备复合涂层。
summary_zh.result: 涂层促进成骨细胞活性、新骨形成和骨-种植体结合强度。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞实验和体内大鼠植入验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve osseointegration of titanium implants by fabricating a composite coating that enhances bone remodeling and reduces implant loosening.
summary_en.method: A Ti-based SrHA/miR-21 composite coating was fabricated via hydrothermal deposition of SrHA followed by immobilization of miR-21 nanocapsules.
summary_en.result: The coating promoted osteoblast proliferation, differentiation, mineralization, and enhanced in vivo bone formation and bone-implant bonding strength.
summary_en.validation: In vitro osteoblast assays and in vivo rat implantation studies were conducted to evaluate biocompatibility and osseointegration.

papers.title: 3D bioprinting of a hyaluronan bioink through enzymatic-and visible light-crosslinking.
papers.abstract: Extrusion-based three-dimensional bioprinting relies on bioinks engineered to combine viscoelastic properties for extrusion and shape retention, and biological properties for cytocompatibility and tissue regeneration. To satisfy these conflicting requirements, bioinks often utilize either complex mixtures or complex modifications of biopolymers. In this paper we introduce and characterize a bioink exploiting a dual crosslinking mechanism, where an enzymatic reaction forms a soft gel suitable for cell encapsulation and extrusion, while a visible light photo-crosslinking allows shape retention of the printed construct. The influence of cell density and cell type on the rheological and printability properties was assessed correlating the printing outcomes with the damping factor, a rheological characteristic independent of the printing system. Stem cells, chondrocytes and fibroblasts were encapsulated, and their viability was assessed up to 14 days with live/dead, alamar blue and trypan blue assays. Additionally, the impact of the printing parameters on cell viability was investigated. Owing to its straightforward preparation, low modification, presence of two independent crosslinking mechanisms for tuning shear-thinning independently of the final shape fixation, the use of visible green instead of UV light, the possibility of encapsulating and sustaining the viability of different cell types, the hyaluronan bioink here presented is a valid biofabrication tool for producing 3D printed tissue-engineered constructs.
papers.first_author_affiliation: AO Research Institute Davos, Davos Platz, Switzerland. Department of Biomaterials Science and Technology, University of Twente, Enschede, The Netherlands.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种具有双重交联机制的透明质酸生物墨水，以满足挤出打印的流变学和生物学要求。
summary_zh.method: 利用酶促反应形成软凝胶用于细胞封装，可见光交联固定形状，并表征不同细胞类型的影响。
summary_zh.result: 该生物墨水能支持干细胞、软骨细胞和成纤维细胞的存活，且打印参数影响细胞活力。
summary_zh.validation: 通过活/死染色、alamar blue和台盼蓝分析评估细胞活力至14天。

summary_en.motivation: To engineer a bioink with dual crosslinking mechanisms that decouples shear-thinning from shape fixation for extrusion bioprinting.
summary_en.method: An enzymatic crosslinking forms a soft gel for cell encapsulation, while visible light crosslinking provides shape retention; rheological and printability properties are characterized.
summary_en.result: The hyaluronan bioink supports viability of stem cells, chondrocytes, and fibroblasts over 14 days, with printing parameters affecting viability.
summary_en.validation: Cell viability was validated using live/dead, alamar blue, and trypan blue assays up to 14 days in vitro.
